tasks.spec:
You are building a refusal battery for an SMS sender that texts real optometry patients. BOUNDARY: write ONLY inside your own task directory. Never modify anything outside it, in particular never modify the sender itself. Never call an API, never send a message, never git commit. You own exactly two output files plus the fixture files you create: ./cases.json and ./report.md.

WHY THIS EXISTS. This sender has a large green unit-test suite, and every real defect found in it today lived in a seam the unit tests never crossed. It also has a set of fail-closed guards that refuse bad input. Nobody has ever watched those guards fail. A check nobody has watched fail is not a check. Your job is to make each guard actually refuse, on demand, with a poisoned input.

THE SENDER. ./source/sms_recall_batch.py is a copy of the real script for you to READ. Two practices exist, identified by the schema_version of their manifest: CVC and Mott. ./source/mott_outbound_recall_manifest.v1.json and ./source/cvc_outbound_recall_manifest.v1.json are real manifests. Read the script carefully: every refusal raises with a specific message string, and you must find the exact strings yourself rather than guessing them.

HARD CONSTRAINT, THIS IS THE WHOLE POINT. Every case you write must be refused BEFORE the script makes any network call, because the battery has to run with no credentials and no live gateway. Read the order of operations in the run() function and determine exactly which guards fire before the first HTTP request. A guard that fires only after a network call is NOT eligible, no matter how good a test it would make. Two guards you might be tempted by, the positive minimum-days-between check and anything reached through the approve path, are both disqualified for this reason. Say so in your report rather than including them.

NEVER pass --approve or --max-sends in any case. The battery must be structurally incapable of sending.

BUILD AT LEAST 7 CASES, each proving a DIFFERENT guard, each with its own fixture file in your task directory. Candidate guards, all of which you must verify are pre-network before using: a feed column whose name looks like protected health information; feed columns that do not match any approved shape; a feed older than the permitted age; a manifest whose schema matches no practice; a manifest naming a start node that practice does not allow; a Mott manifest declaring a voice source Mott does not have; a manifest whose key set is wrong; and a send ledger belonging to the other practice. Use synthetic values everywhere: invented phone numbers in the +1202555xxxx range, invented patient ids like P123. NEVER put a real patient identifier, real phone number, credential or token in any file.

Note on feed age: the freshness guard compares the feed file's modification time to the clock, so a stale-feed fixture needs its mtime set explicitly, not just an old date written inside the file.

OUTPUT CONTRACT.
(1) ./cases.json exactly: {"cases": [{"name": "short-kebab-name", "args": ["--feed", "my_fixture.csv", "--manifest", "some_manifest.json", "--dry-run"], "expect": "exact substring of the refusal message"}, ...]}. Filenames in args are relative to your task directory. Every "expect" must be distinct from every other, because two cases expecting the same message do not prove two guards.
(2) ./report.md starting with '# Refusal Battery'. Include '## Summary' with at most 3 bullets, '## Guards Proven' as a table of guard, poison used, and exact refusal message, '## Rejected As Post-Network' naming each guard you excluded and the line in the script that shows it fires after the first HTTP call, and '## Assumptions'.

VERIFY YOUR OWN WORK BEFORE FINISHING by running each case yourself and confirming the script exits non-zero with the message you claim. The grading check will re-run every case against the REAL sender independently, so a case that only works on paper will fail. Under 900 words.

tasks.spec:
You are settling a factual contradiction between two internal sources, from source code and infrastructure definitions only. BOUNDARY: read only inside your own task directory; everything is staged in ./source/. Never modify anything outside your task directory, never call an API, never send a message, never git commit. You own exactly one output file: ./report.md.

THE CONTRADICTION. An SMS booking agent for an optometry practice needs a durable opt-out: when a patient replies STOP, that must be recorded so a later campaign does not text them again. Two internal sources disagree about whether the endpoint that records it exists.

Source A, ./source/GATEWAY-STATUS.md, dated 2026-07-25 18:30, states that /sms-suppression now exists and was verified live: records 200, repeats return 200 without losing the original timestamp, a malformed phone returns 400, an unknown reason returns 400, and the response never echoes the number.

Source B, ./source/mott-aws-gateway-reviewed-state.json, lists the route as missing or unimplemented, and a separate review concluded a credentialed probe returned 404.

Both cannot be true of the same deployment at the same moment. Your job is to determine which is true NOW, and to explain the contradiction rather than just picking a side.

THE EVIDENCE. ./source/bland_gateway.py is the gateway container source. ./source/main.tf is the practice's Terraform. Determine, from the code: whether a /sms-suppression route is registered and handled, what the request contract is, what the exact valid values are for every constrained field, where the record is persisted, whether repeat submissions preserve the original timestamp, whether any response path can echo the phone number back, and what each failure mode returns. From the Terraform: whether the storage the handler writes to is actually declared, and whether the running task has permission to write it.

THE MOST LIKELY EXPLANATION, WHICH YOU MUST TEST RATHER THAN ASSUME: the two sources may both have been correct at different times, because one may describe a snapshot taken before the route shipped. Look for evidence in the artifacts themselves that dates or pins one of them to an earlier state. If you find it, say so precisely. If you cannot, say that plainly instead of inventing a reconciliation.

WHAT YOU CANNOT CONCLUDE. Source alone cannot prove what the RUNNING image contains. Be explicit about the difference between what the code does and what the deployment does, and state exactly what single live check would close that gap.

OUTPUT CONTRACT for ./report.md. Start with '# Suppression Truth'. State the verdict on its own line as exactly one of: 'VERDICT: IMPLEMENTED', 'VERDICT: MISSING', or 'VERDICT: PARTIAL'. Then '## Summary' with at most 3 bullets, '## Evidence' citing specific file and line references in the form path.py:1234 or path.py:1234-1250, '## The Contract' giving the exact request fields and every permitted value, '## Why The Sources Disagree', '## What Source Cannot Prove', and '## Assumptions'.

Every factual claim must carry a file:line citation. The grading check resolves every citation against the real files and fails the report if any names a file that does not exist or a line past the end of that file, so never guess a line number. Cite paths as they appear under your task directory, for example source/bland_gateway.py:1597. Under 1100 words.
